OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-22: 'we need to be able to verify what's actually trading... it's being operated from our VM, which means there is a single source of truth -- whatever the VM is using is de facto the single source of truth for what's actually trading. And if we can't verify that, then we need to build the mechanism to verify that... there's no reason that that question should just stay open-ended.' AGREED. This row is the mapping, and it exists because I tried to verify R2's cut this session and COULD NOT. [!] THE SIX LAYERS, IN DESCENDING AUTHORITY, EACH WITH WHETHER IT IS READABLE TODAY. (1) THE BROKER -- what positions and orders actually exist at Bybit/Alpaca. Highest authority; nothing on the VM can override it. Readable via /api/bot/positions (unrealizedPnlSource distinguishes broker truth from a local mark) and /api/bot/pnl/broker-truth. AVAILABLE. (2) REALISED BEHAVIOUR -- what the system has actually closed. /api/bot/trades/closed, keyed on `pattern` and `account`. AVAILABLE, and it is the only layer that proves a leg TRADED rather than was configured to. (3) DECISION-LEVEL EMISSIONS -- /api/bot/order-packages and /api/bot/signals. PARTIALLY BROKEN, see the measurements below. (4) THE PROCESS'S LOADED STATE -- pipeline.STRATEGIES and the resolved per-account effective_dry. NOT AVAILABLE AT ALL; this is row E31, and it is the layer the operator's question actually needs. (5) THE FILE ON THE VM -- /api/bot/config, whose mode field is honestly named `yaml_mode`. AVAILABLE, and it is what every reader has been mistaking for layer 4. (6) GIT main. AVAILABLE, and the furthest from the truth. [!] MEASURED THIS SESSION, AND THE HEADLINE IS THAT BEHAVIOURAL VERIFICATION CANNOT WORK FOR A REAL-MONEY BOOK AT TODAY'S TRADE RATE. Population: the 200 most recent closed trades, closedAt 2026-09-13T20:55:29Z -> 2026-09-22T08:48:49Z, about 9 days. Of those, 199 are PAPER and 1 is REAL MONEY -- a single bybit_2/xrp_pullback_2h trade closed 2026-09-14T18:21:48Z, EIGHT DAYS AGO. Trades closed after R2's cut: 2, both bybit_1 (paper), both ict_scalp_*. So when I asked `did any cut leg trade after the cut`, the answer was NONE -- and THE POSITIVE CONTROL FAILED, because no real-money leg traded after the cut either. A negative from a probe whose positive control is silent proves nothing. At a base rate near 0.1 real-money trades/day you would wait weeks for a behavioural answer, and layer 4 is therefore NOT OPTIONAL -- it is the only layer that can answer the question for real money on any useful timescale. [!] TWO DEFECTS FOUND IN LAYER 3 WHILE BUILDING THIS, BOTH THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS. (a) /api/bot/order-packages?limit=201 returns `rows: []` with `count: 0` -- NOT an error and NOT a clamp to the 200 cap. An over-limit request is INDISTINGUISHABLE from `there is no data`, on a read surface the SPA uses. Verified by bisection: limit 50/100/200 return 50/100/200; 201 and 250 return 0. (b) /api/bot/order-packages' newest row is 2026-09-18T15:16:46Z, four days stale, while closed trades exist from today -- so the decision-level surface is NOT tracking what the system is actually doing. (c) /api/bot/signals returns 0 rows under EVERY shape tried (bare, limit=5, limit=50, hours=720, limit=50&hours=2000 -- an 83-day window). I could NOT establish whether that is `no signals` or `a broken read`, and I am not guessing; that distinction is the same defect this row exists to remove. [!] DELIVERABLE: a single documented procedure -- one command or endpoint -- that answers `what is the running trader actually trading right now, and does it match main?`, returning each layer separately with its own read-state, NEVER collapsing `we could not look` into `nothing found`, and REFUSING to return a verdict when the positive control for a behavioural layer is silent. Depends on E31 for layer 4. [!] AND A RULE THAT FALLS OUT OF IT: a Tier-3 roster change is not `done` when the file changes; it is done when layer 4 agrees with layer 6. R2 and B2 are both sitting in exactly that gap right now. [!] OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-09-22, and it narrows this row: 'the roster is not a behaviour-observable fact, it is a LIST-observable fact based on the list that is the single source of truth. Just because something's not trading doesn't mean it's not on the roster -- it could just be sidelined. The only problem we would notice is if we see something trading that's NOT on the roster.' CORRECT, and it means I built the wrong check first. The roster question is answered by READING THE LIST THE VM IS CONFIGURED WITH, not by watching for trades; absence of trading is not absence from the roster, and my behavioural probe was testing a proposition the roster does not make. THE LAYER-2 CHECK IS THEREFORE AN INVERSE ANOMALY DETECTOR, NOT A CONFIRMATION: alert when a leg that is NOT on an account's list closes a trade on it. That is a positive assertion, it needs no positive control, and it fires on the thing that actually matters. [!] AND THE OPERATOR'S SECOND HALF IS THE REAL SPEC: the VM's configuration is the single source of truth and is NOT prescriptive -- so there should be no discrepancy between the list the VM holds and what it routes, and IF THERE IS, THAT IS A BIGGER PROBLEM. So layer 4 (E31) is not there to second-guess the roster; it is there to detect that the process and the file have diverged at all. The measurement that made me build the behavioural check -- 199 paper / 1 real money over 9 days -- was still worth having: it is not a roster fact, it is row E33. MAPPING LANDED in docs/reference/verifying-what-is-trading.md, PR #12738 (draft, with E31 -- one question at two levels, so one PR). [!] LAYER 4 IS NOW MARKED AVAILABLE, and the qualification is the honest part: the code exists and is tested, so it is available ON DEPLOY, not on merge. Until the manager lands and restarts, the live trader's artifact carries no process block -- MEASURED 2026-09-22T12:52:33Z via the relay (issue #12734, run 35729811659) -- and the new reader correctly grades it `not_written`. [!] THE OTHER FIVE LAYERS ARE UNCHANGED AND SAID SO: 1 broker and 2 realised behaviour AVAILABLE, 3 decision-level emissions PARTIALLY BROKEN (the three measured defects from this row are carried verbatim into the doc, including that whether /api/bot/signals' 0 rows means `no signals` or `a broken read` WAS NOT ESTABLISHED and is not being guessed at), 5 the file AVAILABLE, 6 git AVAILABLE. NO LAYER WAS QUIETLY UPGRADED. [!] THE DOC CARRIES SEVEN NAMED THINGS WE STILL CANNOT SEE rather than an implied all-clear, and the biggest is that THE INVERSE ANOMALY DETECTOR IS NOT BUILT -- per the operator's correction, the layer-2 check worth having is `alert when a leg NOT on an account's list closes a trade on it`, which needs no positive control. Layer 4 also covers accounts.yaml + strategies.yaml ONLY; config/pairs.yaml (the isolated M22 order path), regime_policy.yaml and the env surface carry no stamp, and a `current` verdict says nothing about them.
